title: Dhatu Forge
subtitle: Collect roots. Apply transformations. Craft a civilization.

dhr+none.name: Dharma
dhr+none.meaning: That which holds. The structural principle sustaining civilization in coherence - not a law imposed, but the intrinsic holding-pattern of reality.
dhr+none.civ: A civilization built on dharma discovers order rather than legislating it. Law is recognition, not invention.

dhr+sam.name: Saṃdhāraṇa
dhr+sam.meaning: Collective holding. When a community holds together - the bonds that make a people cohere without external coercion.
dhr+sam.civ: The village, the kula, the jāti - social structures that persist through mutual holding, not contract.

dhr+a.name: Ādhāra
dhr+a.meaning: The substrate, the base, the container that holds. The ground on which something rests.
dhr+a.civ: Every concept needs an ādhāra - a ground. Consciousness needs a body. Dharma needs a people. The question is always: what holds what?

r+none.name: Ṛta
r+none.meaning: Cosmic order as movement - the sun moves because it is its nature to move. Order that flows rather than being imposed.
r+none.civ: Before dharma was articulated, there was ṛta. The Ṛgvedic cosmos runs on inherent rhythm, not command.

r+pra.name: Pravṛtti
r+pra.meaning: Forward-movement. Engagement with the world, active participation in the flow of things.
r+pra.civ: Pravṛtti-mārga: the path of engagement. A civilization that honors worldly action as sacred, not merely permitted.

r+vi.name: Nivṛtti
r+vi.meaning: Turning back, withdrawal. The return movement - disengagement from the flow.
r+vi.civ: Nivṛtti-mārga: the path of withdrawal. Sannyāsa is built into the civilizational grammar as the complement to engagement.

kr+none.name: Karma
kr+none.meaning: Action, making, doing. Every act leaves a trace. The universe keeps accounts through the structure of action itself.
kr+none.civ: Karma is not punishment or reward. It is the grammar of action - the fact that doing has consequences encoded in the doing itself.

kr+pra.name: Prakṛti
kr+pra.meaning: The first making. Primordial nature - that which was made before everything else, the material substrate of manifestation.
kr+pra.civ: Sāṃkhya builds its entire cosmology on this: prakṛti as the creative matrix, puruṣa as the witness. The root tells you the relationship.

kr+vi.name: Vikṛti
kr+vi.meaning: Transformation, modification, distortion. What happens when the original making is altered.
kr+vi.civ: Āyurveda diagnoses vikṛti - deviation from prakṛti. Health is return to original making. Disease is distorted action.

sam-kr+none.name: Saṃskāra
sam-kr+none.meaning: Making-well-together. Refinement through collective process. The sixteen life-rites that shape a person from conception to death.
sam-kr+none.civ: Culture (saṃskṛti) is literally 'well-made-together.' A civilization that names itself by its refining process rather than its territory or blood.

sam-kr+pra.name: Saṃskṛti
sam-kr+pra.meaning: Culture, civilization. The collective product of sustained refinement across generations.
sam-kr+pra.civ: Bhārata calls its civilizational identity saṃskṛti - the process of making well. Identity lies in the verb, not the noun.

cit+none.name: Cit / Citta
cit+none.meaning: Consciousness, awareness, the shining-forth of knowing. The field in which all experience arises.
cit+none.civ: A civilization that begins with √cit builds temples oriented inward. Consciousness is primary, matter is derivative.

cit+pra.name: Praciti
cit+pra.meaning: Recognition, conviction. Consciousness directed forward - the flash of knowing that hits.
cit+pra.civ: Yogic pratyaya: the moment consciousness grasps its object with certainty. The epistemology is built into the root.

cit+vi.name: Vicitra
cit+vi.meaning: Variegated, wonderful, manifold. Consciousness dispersed into multiplicity.
cit+vi.civ: The world's beauty is vi-cit: consciousness scattered into endless forms. Aesthetics encoded in a prefix.

man+none.name: Manas
man+none.meaning: Mind, the thinking instrument. Not consciousness itself but the tool consciousness uses to think.
man+none.civ: Manas is not ātman. The mind is an instrument, not the self. This distinction - which English collapses - generates the entire yogic project.

man+pra.name: Pramāṇa
man+pra.meaning: Means of valid knowledge. The measure by which knowing is measured.
man+pra.civ: Every darśana begins by declaring its pramāṇas. Epistemology before metaphysics - you must know how you know before you claim what is.

man+sam.name: Sammati
man+sam.meaning: Consensus, agreement, common thinking. When minds come together.
man+sam.civ: Governance by sammati - thinking-together - rather than voting or decree. The sabha tradition.

bhr+none.name: Bhārata
bhr+none.meaning: The one who bears, nourishes, maintains. The name of the civilization - 'those who bear/nourish.'
bhr+none.civ: A civilization that names itself 'the bearers' - those who carry and nourish the tradition forward. Identity as responsibility.

bhr+sam.name: Saṃbhāra
bhr+sam.meaning: Provisions, materials gathered together. The collecting of what is needed.
bhr+sam.civ: Before any yajña, the saṃbhāra must be gathered. Civilization requires material preparation alongside spiritual intent.

pu+none.name: Pūjā / Pāvana
pu+none.meaning: Purification, worship as purification, merit as the purified residue of right action.
pu+none.civ: Worship is purification. Puṇya is what remains when the impure is burned away. The sacred is the clean.

pu+vi.name: Vipāvana
pu+vi.meaning: Thorough purification, complete cleansing. The intensified purificatory act.
pu+vi.civ: Prāyaścitta - the restoration of purity after transgression. A civilization that encodes recovery, not permanent damnation.

brh+none.name: Brahman
brh+none.meaning: The expansive. That which grows without limit. The absolute as boundless expansion.
brh+none.civ: The highest reality named by a verb of growth. Brahman is not a static absolute - it is ceaseless expansion.

brh+pra.name: Prabṛhaṇa
brh+pra.civ: The brāhmaṇa's function: to expand knowledge. The priest is named for what the root does - grows the sacred.

at+none.name: Atithi
at+none.meaning: The one who wanders, the guest. One who arrives without fixed schedule (a-tithi: without a date).
at+none.civ: Atithi devo bhava: the wanderer is god. A civilization that sacralizes the unexpected arrival - hospitality encoded in the root of movement.

at+pra.name: Praṭana
at+pra.meaning: Going forth, wandering with purpose. The directed journey.
at+pra.civ: Tīrtha-yātrā: the sacred wandering. Movement itself as spiritual practice, not mere transit.

yaj+none.name: Yajña
yaj+none.meaning: Offering, exchange, sacrifice. The cosmic transaction that sustains the world.
yaj+none.civ: Yajña is the operating logic of the Vedic cosmos. Gods and humans sustain each other through reciprocal offering. The universe runs on exchange, not extraction.

yaj+pra.name: Prayāja
yaj+pra.meaning: The preliminary offering. What must be offered first before the main act begins.
yaj+pra.civ: Every endeavor requires a prayāja - an initial giving-up before receiving. The grammar of preparation.

yaj+upa.name: Upayāja
yaj+upa.meaning: Subsidiary offering. The supporting sacrifice that makes the main one possible.
yaj+upa.civ: Nothing stands alone. Every central act has upayājas - supporting structures. Civilization as layered offering.

yantr+none.name: Yantra
yantr+none.meaning: That which channels, restrains, holds in form. Instrument, machine, sacred diagram.
yantr+none.civ: A yantra channels cosmic energy into form. Technology and sacred geometry share a root - both are instruments of channeling.

yantr+sam.name: Saṃyama
yantr+sam.meaning: Total restraint. In yoga: dhāraṇā + dhyāna + samādhi held together.
yantr+sam.civ: Patañjali's saṃyama: the three highest limbs fused. Mastery is channeling held steady. The yogi as living yantra.

smr+none.name: Smṛti
smr+none.meaning: Memory, remembered tradition. What the civilization carries forward through human recall.
smr+none.civ: Smṛti is law that changes with memory - adaptable, era-specific. The tradition distinguishes what is heard (permanent) from what is remembered (contextual).

smr+pra.name: Prasmṛti
smr+pra.meaning: Deep remembrance, recollection. Memory that reaches back to origin.
smr+pra.civ: Itihāsa: 'so indeed it was.' History as deep remembrance, not documentation. The civilization trusts trained memory over inscription.

shru+none.name: Śruti
shru+none.meaning: That which is heard. Revelation received through listening - the Vedas as heard truth.
shru+none.civ: The highest authority is not written or reasoned - it is heard. A civilization that places listening above argumentation as the route to truth.

shru+pra.name: Praśruti
shru+pra.meaning: Fame, renown - that which is heard widely. When what you are is heard across distance.
shru+pra.civ: Reputation as 'being heard far.' Character produces resonance. Dharmic fame is not self-promotion but audibility of virtue.

shru+upa.name: Upaniṣad
shru+upa.meaning: Sitting close to listen. The knowledge transmitted in proximity - guru to śiṣya.
shru+upa.civ: The highest texts named for a posture of listening. Knowledge requires nearness. Truth is not broadcast - it is whispered to the ready ear.

jiv+none.name: Jīva
jiv+none.meaning: The living one, the life-principle. Individual soul as the one who lives.
jiv+none.civ: Jīva is not 'soul' as substance but 'the living' as verb-become-noun. You are not a thing that has life - you are the living itself.

jiv+pra.name: Prājīvya
jiv+pra.meaning: Livelihood, the means by which one lives forward.
jiv+pra.civ: Vṛtti - livelihood - is a dharmic category. How you sustain life is not secular but sacred. Economics as a branch of dharma.

mr+none.name: Mṛtyu
mr+none.meaning: Death as dissolution. Not ending but un-making - the return to unformed state.
mr+none.civ: Death is √mṛ: dissolution, not extinction. What was made (√kṛ) is un-made. Rebirth follows because making never stops.

mr+pra.name: Pralaya
mr+pra.meaning: The great dissolution. Cosmic death - when everything returns to the unmanifest.
mr+pra.civ: Pralaya is not apocalypse. It is rest between creations. The cosmos breathes: sṛṣṭi (emission) and pralaya (reabsorption). Death at cosmic scale is a pause.

mr+vi.name: Vimukti
mr+vi.meaning: Liberation, release. The final dissolution of bondage.
mr+vi.civ: Mokṣa is a form of dying - dying to saṃsāra while alive. Liberation is death done right, on purpose.
